messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty INC-2026-42 fired for embeddings-service (eu-west-1). Severity: P2. Alerts: embeddings.p95>5s, embeddings.5xx_rate spike. Auto-page to oncall group.
maria: I'm primary on this. Brief: after a k8s rolling upgrade started ~30m ago in eu-west, we've seen KV cache eviction storms on the embeddings sidecars which is causing high backend retries and 500s. Affected customers: a handful of mid-market customers using synchronous embeddings and the batch pipeline.

Impact summary: ~12% of embedding requests returning 500s, p95 latency ~3x baseline for eu-west, other regions nominal. No data loss, requests are failing fast.

sam: I can jump in as secondary. I have infra access and can scale node pool if needed. Noted that autoscaler has been inactive during the node drain window.

maria: Current mitigations in progress: toggled fallback routing for embeddings to route eu-west traffic to eu-central for low-priority customers (non-SLA) and limited batch ingestion; rolled back the newest sidecar image on two of the pods; increased KV cache size on one node as an experiment.

Commands run (by me):
```
# scale up the eu-west node pool temporarily
gcloud container clusters resize eu-west-cluster --node-pool=embed-pool --num-nodes=8
# rollback sidecar image on deployments
kubectl -n inference set image deploy/embeddings-sidecar embeddings-sidecar=registry.redwood/sidecar:2026-03-05-rollback
```

jon: Logged into the node and saw repeated OOM+eviction events in /var/log/kubelet.log for the embed pods. Kernel OOM killer is triggering after the node drain. Could be memory pressure + a missed resource limit on a new image.

lee: I grabbed the logs and pushed a short excerpt to the incident thread:
```
[2026-04-14T20:12:03Z] eviction: process "embed-worker" invoked oom_kill, rss=7.8G
[2026-04-14T20:12:07Z] kubelet: evicting pods to reclaim memory: embeddings-sidecar-abc123
```

maria: Runbook pointers: follow "KV cache thrash" runbook -> https://internal.redwood/runbooks/kv-cache-thrash (steps 1-5 have checklist). Also check the embeddings playbook for fallback routing -> https://internal.redwood/playbooks/embeddings-fallback.

incident-bot: Added annotation: runbook:kv-cache-thrash. PagerDuty assignee: maria.

sam: Short-term plan: 1) Keep routing fallback to eu-central for non-SLA traffic. 2) Spin up 2 additional nodes in eu-west and cordon the upgraded nodes. 3) Force-evict the rolling upgrade until we can confirm sidecar resource limits. 4) If repeated OOM, rollback the node image.

maria: I've asked infra to provision +2 nodes (ticket INFRA-3645). If infra can't provision within 15m, we consider scaling down the drain parallelism.

kai: FYI I'll be on PTO starting 23:00 UTC for ~2 hours. I won't be able to take secondary pager during that window.

maria: Noted. That means we have a coverage gap 23:00-01:00 UTC unless someone picks up. Sam — can you be primary at 20:40 UTC and keep watching through the gap? If not, we need a volunteer.

sam: I can be primary starting 20:40 UTC for the next 3 hours. I'll hand back at 00:00 UTC to jon if needed.

jon: I'll stay shadowing and handle infra escalations if autoscaler or node group fails. I'll also run the healthcheck script every 5m:
```
#!/bin/bash
# quick healthcheck for embeddings in eu-west
kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=embeddings -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}: {.status.containerStatuses[0].state.waiting.reason}\n'
```

maria: Outstanding asks for next shift (sam primary):
- Confirm INFRA-3645 completes and nodes land in pool.
- If 5xx rate stays >8% for >30m, escalate to infra lead and consider complete rollback of the node pool.
- Monitor customer-impact dashboard and message customers@realtime if regression persists >60m. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/d/embeddings/eu-west-summary

lee: Also add a quick mitigation: if we see more than 3 OOMs in a host within 10m, run: `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data <node>` to stop scheduling and reduce pressure. Use with care.

maria: I'll update the incident doc with timeline and cross-link to the RTR notes. Leaving handoff now — Sam will be primary in 20m. Jon is secondary, Lee is on-call infra. Kai is unavailable 23:00-01:00 UTC (coverage gap).

maria: Short status at handoff: mitigations active (routing fallback + partial rollback), infra provisioning in progress, customer impact reduced from 12% -> ~7% after partial actions but still above target.

sam: Taking primary in 20m. ping me directly for escalations @sam. I'll post a watch-confirm message when nodes are up.

jon: I'll be on standby for infra escalations. Leaving a note in the incident doc: "if infra can't scale, swap routing to global fallback permanently until next maintenance window."

maria: Thanks team. Leaving the thread — will check back in 60m. :thumbsup:
